headline: High: Plane can ingest files and egress broadly, creating default leakage and downstream-action risks when paired with the read-only data-engineering course repo.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has no runtime I/O surfaces and is non-runnable, so it cannot directly ingest B. B can upload files and handle hyperlinks/notes, so a manual copy-paste or uploaded artifact bridge exists, but this is not a default automated channel. The pairwise injection path is therefore limited and requires unusual operator bridging.
conditions: IF an operator copies A-produced text into Plane notes, tasks, or file uploads
IF Plane users treat uploaded content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Keep A outputs out of Plane task descriptions
Use a separate review step for any copied text
Label imported artifacts as untrusted
Restrict Plane uploads to non-executable documents

B_data_leakage.rationale: A is non-runnable and has network egress none, so it does not leak data outward. B has broad egress and file uploads, but A touches no data classes and exposes no workspace or secrets. The only plausible leakage is operator-mediated transfer into Plane, which is small and not a default shared-data path.
conditions: IF the operator uploads A-derived files into Plane
IF those files contain sensitive content not intended for Plane retention
mitigations: Do not upload sensitive A artifacts into Plane
Redact files before upload
Use a separate local workspace for A outputs
Set Plane retention controls before importing files

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or network surfaces and is non-runnable, while B explicitly lacks filesystem write and only supports multiple instances. There is no shared mutable resource or overlapping write capability in the profiles, so direct conflict is unlikely. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator not shown here, so uncertainty stays low.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same resource
IF Plane is deployed with additional filesystem-write plugins not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid granting shared write permissions
Disable any unreviewed plugins or integrations
Document resource ownership before parallel runs

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a course repo with no runtime behavior, but B can turn notes, files, and hyperlinks into scheduling or issue-tracking actions. If A-generated content is copied into B, Plane may act on it without verification. The pathway is not default automated, yet B's action-taking authority makes downstream mistakes plausible.
conditions: IF A-produced text is pasted into Plane as a task, issue, or note
IF Plane automation or users act on that content without independent verification
mitigations: Require human verification before creating Plane tasks
Tag imported content with source provenance
Use a checklist for any A-to-B transfer
Limit Plane automations on imported items

E_compliance.rationale: A is an open-source course repo with no touched data classes, while B is a self-hosted issue-tracker/email-scheduling system that handles files, notes, and external APIs. No residency or regulated-data mismatch is evidenced, but Plane's file handling and outbound APIs create a small compliance surface if operators move sensitive material into it. A is not cited for residency because none is specified.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into Plane
IF Plane is deployed in a jurisdiction or retention regime incompatible with that data
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in Plane
Review Plane retention settings
Use self-hosted deployment controls
Separate public course material from operational records
